# runtimeconditions-source-control

Use this extension when your workload works with a Git repository while it runs, for example a build
tool that clones code, or a bot that pushes changes.

In a Condition, you say which Git host the workload uses, and what it does with the repository: clone,
fetch, pull or push. The platform then gives the workload access that allows exactly these actions.
Right now the only host is GitHub.

```sh
pip install runtimeconditions-source-control
```

Runtime Conditions extension: https://runtimeconditions.io/extensions/rc/source-control/0.2.0/runtimeconditions.extension.yaml

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `access` | `Access` | yes | What your workload does with the repository. List every action that it needs. clone, fetch, pull or push. List at least one, each one once.<br>Values:<br>`clone`: Make a copy of the repository.<br>`fetch`: Download new changes, without changing the local files.<br>`pull`: Download new changes and add them to the local files.<br>`push`: Send local changes back to the repository. |
| `provider` | `Provider` | yes | The service that hosts the repository. Right now this is always github. Always github.<br>Values:<br>`github`: The repository is on GitHub. |

</details>

## rc_source_control

`rc_source_control` declares a `rc.source_control` Condition.

Your workload needs access to a Git repository.

Example: a build tool that clones a repository on GitHub and fetches new changes.

```python
from runtimeconditions_source_control import (
    AccessItem,
    Git,
    Provider,
    rc_source_control,
)

rc_source_control(
    Git(access=[AccessItem.CLONE, AccessItem.FETCH], provider=Provider.GITHUB),
)
```

In a Profile, this declares:

```yaml
kind: rc.source_control
interface:
  type: git
  provider: github
  access: [clone, fetch]
```

Every class, field and enum member is documented in the package's docstrings.
